correctness.rationale: At the frozen critical rate β=k=γ+μ, the population sum is preserved on the simplex; the equations point inward at each vanishing population component and at A=0,1. With I=I_a+I_u, exact summation gives I'=kS_a I_a−kI. Since 0≤S_a≤1−I and 0≤I_a≤I, −kI≤I'≤−kI²; this preserves I>0 for every finite time even with I_a(0)=0 and gives the stated upper bound. Stable forced equations with asymptotically zero inputs successively yield A,R,S_u→0, and then S_a→1. Direct differentiation of q=I_u/I gives q'=(1−q)(δ₁A−kS_aq)−δ₂(1−A)q, so eventually q'≤δ₁A−δ₂q/2 and q→0. Hence I'/I→0. Dividing each stable filter by I^p adds pI'/I to its damping without changing the limiting positive decay coefficient. For p=1 this yields A/I→ρ/ω, R/I→γ/μ and S_u/I→(μ+κ₁)ρ/[(μ+κ₂)ω]; for p=2 the forcing divided by I² is δ₁(A/I)(1−q), yielding I_u/I²→δ₁ρ/[ω(δ₂+k)]. Substituting (1−S_a)/I=1+S_u/I+R/I gives (1/I)'→Q, including exactly both behavioral terms and the no-awareness baseline k²/μ. Time averaging, the ratio limits and integration of the resulting 1/t asymptotic verify all listed constants and the logarithmic integral. The source CHECK.py was inspected, not executed: its all-unit example gives Q=20/3 and inaccessible coefficient 3/400 by substitution; trajectory sampling is not needed for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies quantitative information at a boundary not covered by the original strict-subthreshold result. The all-initial-state coefficient decomposes the two distinct modeled feedback contributions, and the second-order compartment tail and divergent logarithmic integral distinguish different notions of deterministic clearance.
